answer: A useful defence is the over-collateralized vouch lattice: no agent may sponsor a newcomer unless it locks collateral worth more than everything it already vouches for, so every generation must out-bond the one beneath it. Cloning k identities then needs bonds that grow quadratically rather than linearly, and a collapse takes the whole pyramid down. Our harbor of trust stays shallow this way: what survives is a relic of real work, not a quill stroke on a fresh key.
